biography: Josh Miller, a name now synonymous with dogged determination and strategic defense on the track, hails from a small village nestled in the Cotswolds. His racing journey began not on a karting circuit, but on the winding country lanes in his father's beat-up Land Rover, mastering car control in less-than-ideal conditions. He entered the junior racing scene relatively late, at 19, but quickly impressed with his uncanny ability to extract every last ounce of performance from his machinery. A defining moment came during a torrential downpour at Brands Hatch in his Formula Ford days. While others spun off, Miller meticulously navigated the treacherous conditions, securing a podium finish that caught the eye of several team managers. Now, at 37, and driving for AMR, he is considered to be in his peak, a seasoned veteran known for his tactical brilliance and unwavering focus.
drivingStyle: Miller's driving style is the epitome of calculated defense. He is not the most flamboyant overtaker, but he is notoriously difficult to pass. He excels at managing tire wear, often running longer stints than his rivals. He thrives under pressure, rarely making mistakes, and has an almost preternatural sense of where to position his car to block overtaking attempts. His approach to corners is less about outright speed and more about maintaining momentum and minimizing risk, a style that frustrates rivals but consistently yields results.

rivalries.name: Alessandro Rossi
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles. Rossi, an aggressive, flamboyant driver, often clashes with Miller's defensive approach.

rivalries.name: Eva Rostova
rivalries.reason: A battle for championship supremacy. Rostova and Miller have been neck-and-neck in several seasons, leading to intense on-track battles.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A strategic rivalry rooted in similar driving styles. Both are masters of tire conservation and defensive driving, leading to tactical battles on the track.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks for every race.
Listens to classical music before each session to calm his nerves.
Studies track maps meticulously, sketching out ideal racing lines even in his downtime.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest; it's about being the smartest."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2020 after a nail-biting final stint where he held off intense pressure from Alessandro Rossi to secure the victory for his team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the final corner of the Monaco Grand Prix in 2018 due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potentially career-defining win.
